PUBLIC LAUNCH · V1.0.0-RC.99 · 2026-10-24

RC.99: SMART, RESOURCE-AWARE AUTOINDEX
AND MORE HARNESS TOOLS.

XERJ ENGINEERING · PUBLISHED 2026-10-24

v1.0.0-rc.99 is the public launch. Autoindex in this cut respects the machine it is running on. It drains memtable pressure on the 8 GiB step, and a host under 16 GiB takes half of its RAM as the cap. It packs embeddings so a JSONL corpus does not keep a number tree in memory, streams or skips an oversized JSON document, and prints a neural embedding estimate before the run starts. The harness gained definition lookup, ordered batch retrieval, a search prefix, and matched-line citations, plus a DeepSeek Harness profile bundle and a Cline row that has now been run. It is also the 98th tagged v1.0.0-rc.* release. 97 tags exist through rc.98, because rc.79 was never tagged. It lands just over 100 days since rc.1.

01 · THE MACHINE

Autoindex that stays inside the box you gave it

A laptop and a large server do not get the same budget. Hosts at 16 GiB and above keep the stepped cap: 8 GiB below 64 GiB, then 16 GiB and 32 GiB. On the 8 GiB step the summed memtable budget is 2 GiB (25% of the cap, floored at 2 GiB) while each index still flushes at 512 MiB by default. A corpus spread across dozens of indices crosses the process budget with every index under its own flush line. Writes stay HTTP 429 and the indexed count stays 0. The sampler now requests a drain when that summed-memtable latch is engaged, on the same interval as the RSS latch. A bulk the parent breaker has not accepted a single item from stops at 90 seconds, and the terminal line names limits.max_process_memory_mb (#2244).

8 GiB
step from 16 GiB to 64 GiB
Hosts at 16 GiB and above. Under 16 GiB the default cap is half of RAM. An 8 GiB machine gets 4 GiB.
2 GiB
memtable budget on that tier
25% of the 8 GiB cap. Pressure on this sum now drains, so a multi-index corpus can make progress.
8 MiB
one JSON document
Past this ceiling the document is skipped or refused. The ceiling is fixed.
64 MiB
uncompressed JSON, streamed
A file over the old whole-file cap is walked from disk. Gzip still uses the in-memory cap.

Embeddings are packed. A semantic_text vector is stored as one xerj:f32: hex string. GET and _source expand it back to a number array on the page that is returned. kNN and HNSW read the same bits. Both memtables used to keep the JSON number tree until flush, which is what let JSONL autoindex resident memory grow with the corpus (#2240).

One oversized JSON document is streamed or refused. A single document over 8 MiB is not indexed, so one large file does not have to be parsed and tokenized inside one request. Autoindex streams a top-level array, or a top-level array of records, one element at a time, and skips only the values over that ceiling. The skip names the file. A bulk item over the limit is HTTP 413, and its neighbours still index. The ceiling is a fixed constant. It is not raised by --max-file-mb or limits.max_process_memory_mb (#2256).

The node reserves memory for a bulk before it parses one. Before a raw batch is parsed, the engine reserves 28 bytes per input byte against live process memory and against reservations already held, and rechecks the add so two bulks cannot both pass the same snapshot. A batch that would reach the watermark is HTTP 429 circuit_breaking_exception before the WAL append. An uncompressed .json file over 64 MiB is walked from disk, one document-sized value at a time, instead of being refused unread. Gzip stays on the in-memory cap, because the uncompressed length is not known until the bytes are inflated (#2302).

#2256, #2302, #2236, #2340, #2322, and #2315 improve #1122. That issue stays open. The memory-ceiling class and the WSL2 VM death are not addressed by #2340, #2322, or #2315.

A full memtable budget flushes. When the process memtable budget is full, autoindex no longer sits on HTTP 429 until it gives up. The rejection requests a drain, largest memtable first, instead of waiting for the next memory sample. A search issued while that breaker is engaged publishes those memtables before it scans them, so the search does not stall. xerj search and xerj def saying no indices named … name the prefixes on the node in that same line, including a prefix recorded only on a catalog dataset document (#2325 fixes #2321).

An idle node stops draining. A node whose resident set sits flat at or above the watermark no longer drains every 2 seconds for the rest of the process. The breaker releases once RSS has not fallen by more than 4 MiB for 2 seconds, and does not re-arm inside that band. A climb past it engages again. While it stays engaged, drain spacing doubles up to 15 minutes when a drain does not lower RSS by more than 4 MiB. corpus index and autoindex report eta_quality=stalled when a phase with a known total completes nothing, including 0/N, and when a phase with no total has been silent for 10 minutes (#2232 fixes #1981).

Under 16 GiB, the cap is half of RAM. An 8 GiB machine used to take the 8 GiB step, so the budget was the whole machine. A merge storm on Windows 10 stayed up only after XERJ_MAX_PROCESS_MEMORY_MB=4096. That host now gets a 4 GiB cap. A merge batch on a budget that cannot hold the historical 512 MiB input (8× working set plus the 2 GiB memtable floor) is sized to budget / 64 (64 MiB at 4 GiB), and concurrent merges share a quarter of the budget. A batch that would still cross the RSS watermark waits. One batch still runs. Hosts at 16 GiB and above keep the 8 / 16 / 32 GiB steps, the 512 MiB batch, and the configured merge parallelism. A single JSON document over 50 MiB is still refused at the 8 MiB ceiling before it is parsed, and the rest of the bulk is indexed. This improves #1122. That issue stays open (#2340).

A refused thread or a huge update no longer aborts the process. Indexing workers, sync replay, object-watch fetches, and mailbox parsers start with pthread_create and do not map an alternate signal stack. A spawn the OS refuses is an error: the job does not run, workers already started keep going, and the caller runs the work on the calling thread or records the failure. An update body over two 8 MiB documents plus 256 KiB of envelope is refused before serde_json, and the existing document is left as it was. This improves #1122. That issue stays open (#2322).

A helper thread or a merge buffer that cannot be allocated no longer aborts the node. An in-process shard call starts its 8 MiB thread with pthread_create. If the OS refuses, it returns could not start the shard call without running the handler. PUT /{index}/_doc/{id} and PUT /{index}/_create/{id} refuse a body over the 8 MiB ceiling before parsing, the same way POST /{index}/_doc already did. A merge that cannot reserve its output buffer, document map, or the next survivor keeps the input segments and stays up. PDF and .xls output readers, the autoindex progress ticker, and the finalize-verify search use the same fallible spawn. This improves #1122. That issue stays open (#2315).

A killed corpus index resumes. A kill after indices exist and before the ledger is written used to re-hash the corpus under a different prefix, and xerj code then said no verified build was recorded. The command now finds that build's journal and resumes it (#2243).

Windows sizes the cap from commit space. The auto tier is still chosen from physical RAM. On Windows a second ceiling then applies: what this process can still reach, min(commit limit, process commit + available commit), minus a reserve of one quarter of that amount, clamped to 512 MiB–2 GiB. A pagefile that covers RAM does not move the 64 GiB and 128 GiB tier steps. The report behind the change is a 16 GiB machine with no pagefile (#2174, #2236). This is part of the same open issue, #1122.

A full disk says so in one sentence. A memory write blocked at the flood-stage watermark used to surface as a nested cluster_block_exception. The client now turns that block into one sentence: the disk holding the data dir is nearly full, with free space, used percent, the threshold, the data-dir path, and the recovery (free space, or restart with --data-dir on another drive). A reason that already says this is left as it is. An explicit index.blocks.write stays the original error (#2290).

Neural embedding time is estimated before the run. When the server has measured a probe, autoindex prints how long embedding the source that feeds a semantic_text dataset should take, from that probe's passages, bytes, and milliseconds. The figure comes from the probe. No probe, a zero probe, or a non-neural backend prints no duration. The same note says --embed-mode is fixed per index at ingest: changing the flag leaves documents already written as they are, and a new index is how you re-embed. The default embedder is lexical feature-hashing unless the node was started with --embed-mode neural (#2250).

index.default_pipeline survives a restart. Create stored the binding in settings.json, and GET /_settings still reported it after a clean restart, but an ordinary document write no longer ran the pipeline. Opening an existing index now copies that file into the in-memory map before the index is visible. Explicit ?pipeline= was already working. index.final_pipeline is not a setting this build reads (#2296).

_refresh no longer stalls behind a merge. The handler used to flush every matching index in turn, including verified WAL maintenance when the memtable was already empty. A wildcard refresh at the end of autoindex sat behind the first index whose durability tail was slow, and a merge encode held a blocking thread for the whole encode. Matching indices now refresh together. An empty memtable returns without that WAL maintenance. A merge encode is queued on the merge pool. A refresh that still has a memtable to publish stays inside the existing flush admission and caller budgets (#2245).

PDF and .xls workers start on macOS 27. xerj autoindex no longer junks every PDF on an OS that rejects setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS). macOS 27 returns EINVAL. A hard limit below 1536 MiB returns EPERM. The address-space cap is crash isolation: the refusal is logged once and the worker still starts. Linux still applies the 1536 MiB cap. The same refusal is ignored for the isolated .xls reader. If every PDF fails because the worker could not start, the run finishes ok=false exit=1 reason=pdf-worker-unavailable instead of looking like completed-with-junk (#2338 fixes #2336).

.sql schema files are indexed as code. CREATE TABLE, VIEW, FUNCTION, PROCEDURE, INDEX, TRIGGER, TYPE, SCHEMA, and SEQUENCE become symbols, and the source stays searchable. A comment, a quoted literal, a dollar-quoted body, or an INSERT or COPY nested inside another statement is not a dump. Those files used to be sniffed as an empty SQL dump and skipped (no records extracted), which dropped hand-written DDL. A file with a top-level INSERT … VALUES is still a row dump. A data-only COPY … FROM stdin dump is skipped with that reason. When the same file also contains schema statements, those statements are indexed as code (#2342 fixes #2337).

Graph mode re-indexes a folder after files change. An added file that fits a frozen dataset is indexed on the rerun. A file that needs a new dataset stays unindexed until --fresh. Documents, catalog rows, and graph edges for a file that left the folder are removed, and the run names that file, including when --fresh rebuilds the plan. xerj autoindex remove deletes that folder's resume journal and sync-snapshots. An explicit --state-dir on remove deletes the journal there too. A file whose size changes while a run is reading it is skipped with a warning instead of aborting, on the graph path and on --no-graph snapshot sealing. A rerun that removes documents for files that left finishes exit 3 (reason=files-removed). The next unchanged rerun is exit 0 (#2317 fixes #2314).

A proxy embedder resumes. Semantic xerj autoindex against --embed-mode proxy resumes after a mid-run failure and does not re-embed documents already indexed, when the backend, configured model, endpoint, and confirmed vector width are unchanged. The proxy digest is still the model and endpoint (#533). The width is learned with one probe, remembered under the data directory, and compared on resume, so a successful probe does not change the hash an existing index was recorded under. A proxy whose endpoint has not confirmed a width stays non-resumable. The refusal says to make the endpoint reachable and rerun (already-indexed documents are kept) or to rebuild with a new --state-dir and --prefix only to discard the corpus. A provider that swaps weights without changing the name, endpoint, or width is still not detectable (#2307 fixes #2306).

02 · HARNESS TOOLS

Definitions, batch retrieval, a prefix, a line number

MCP xerj_def (#2166) is local definition lookup. It takes symbol, prefix or index, kind, lang, k from 1 to 50, and max_tokens. No match is a successful empty hit list. Invalid arguments are rejected before any HTTP request. With neither prefix nor index, it searches ax-*.

MCP xerj_search accepts prefix (#2137). {"prefix":"project","query":"retry policy"} searches project-*. The default with neither index nor prefix remains ax-*. An empty prefix, a prefix that cannot name an index, or index and prefix together is rejected before HTTP.

A hit can name the matched line. xerj_search used to report only the passage start_line, so an agent citing file:line had to count lines inside the passage. Plain queries now stamp match_line and a capped match_lines on each hit. match_line is the absolute 1-based source line of the best-scoring whole-word query term inside the passage. A tie takes the earliest line. xerj search prints the same annotation as path:match_line. Both fields are omitted when no term is located or the passage start line is unknown. start_line stays the passage start (#2269).

DeepSeek Harness has a profile bundle, and the row is untested. #2298 adds dsh/. It does not start a node and does not replace xerj mcp. It inserts one @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client plugin, with command: xerj so the bundle does not hard-code a machine path. The README's supported-agents table still marks that row untested: the path and shape are transcribed from the client's own documentation, and nobody has run it yet. XERJ is not in a DeepSeek directory.

Cline is marked tested. #2300. Cline CLI 3.0.73 on Linux registered xerj mcp from the README's mcpServers block, against xerj v1.0.0-rc.98. xerj_search appeared in the tool list Cline handed the model, and Cline executed one xerj_search call. The model turn was a local OpenAI-compatible stub, because no provider key was available. The IDE's MCP Servers > Configure button was not part of that run. OpenCode was already the other tested row. The README's definition of tested is that the server was registered and xerj_search appeared in the tool list.

xerj batch-search and MCP xerj_batch_search. xerj batch-search --input <file|-> and the MCP tool retrieve up to 50 IDs or questions in input order through one _msearch call. Each item returns cited evidence, an explicit empty-result abstention, or an independent error. Exact IDs require an indexed keyword field. Optional whole-response token budgets preserve outcomes and at least one citation per matched item, or refuse explicitly. This is retrieval, not generated answers or calibrated confidence. It is a partial implementation of #1801 (#2333, Jarvis636431).

A multi-term question ranks coverage. A question with three or more content tokens no longer ranks a one-word symbol definition (type Token) above a hit that covers more of the question. xerj search, xerj def, xerj code, and the plain-string xerj_search tool add that coverage score and drop a one-term name-and-kind hit behind those results. A one-token lookup (xerj def Token) is unchanged. A nested test callback larger than a passage is no longer returned whole: the line-snapped window is kept, with its line. An archived path (archive/, archived/, or keep_archived) is marked on the xerj code header and on xerj search (#2329 fixes #2327).

xerj corpus add --own marks first-party code. xerj corpus add --own and xerj corpus own <name> (--off clears it) set "own": true in corpus.json. xerj code and MCP xerj_code_search still name an unidentified licence (UNKNOWN or NONE-FOUND) on each hit and omit the do-not-copy banner for that unidentified licence. A licence the detector actually named still warns. A local path is not marked own unless the flag is passed, and a --from manifest cannot set the marker. xerj corpus index prints a per-file-class indexed versus ignored-data summary at the end (#2343 fixes #2339).

03 · ALSO IN THIS CUT

CPUs without AVX2, cluster writes on the primary, one semantic skip

x86_64 binaries no longer require AVX2 (#2253, #2161). The release baseline is x86-64-v2 (SSE4.2: Nehalem and later, Bulldozer and later). The HNSW eight-accumulator dot product is compiled again with AVX2 and FMA enabled and selected at runtime when the CPU has both. The source does not use an explicit FMA, so that compilation is bit-identical to the scalar one. Installers install on a CPU without AVX2. XERJ_SKIP_CPU_CHECK is gone. A CPU without SSE4.2 still cannot run the binary. Field report #2158 is an Intel Core i3-3110M, Ivy Bridge, which has no AVX2.

Cluster replication moved further on the data plane. #1170 stays open. A single node is unchanged: with no cluster handle, writes and search stay on the node that received them.

  • #2257 proposes index create, delete, mapping, and settings through the Raft log when a cluster handle is attached. The HTTP call succeeds after this node has applied the committed entry. A follower forwards to the leader.
  • #2271 puts one primary per member into that same create entry. Member ids are sorted. GET, PUT, and POST of one document, and DELETE /{index}/_doc/{id}, run on that owner. A search of one concrete index asks every owner.
  • #2287 copies an acknowledged document write onto replicas before the caller is answered. index.number_of_replicas at create places those copies on the next members in the ring, wrapping, never on the primary, and capped at one less than the member count. An absent setting places zero replicas. The bytes live in a hidden index, .xerj_replica_{index}_{shard}, so a search fan-out does not count a document twice.
  • #2303 acknowledges a document write at a majority of the copies placed at create (copies / 2 + 1), and the primary counts. With two replicas, the primary plus one replica is enough. The replica that does not confirm is removed from the in-sync set before the caller is answered. The primary alone, when two replicas were placed, is still HTTP 503 replica_not_acknowledged. Zero or one replica is unchanged: that one replica must still confirm.
  • #2313 opens an on-disk Raft log at {data_dir}/_raft when clustering is enabled, and replays its committed prefix before the node serves. A restart restores the shard plan and the in-sync set, so a later document write is routed to the primary again. A member that starts with an empty log copies the leader's log and applies it. Documents written before it joined are copied by the backfill below. Term and vote are stored with the log. Clustering disabled does not open the log.
  • #2320 compacts that log once 64 metadata entries have been applied since the previous snapshot. The compacted prefix is stored in {data_dir}/_raft/snapshot.meta and removed from raft.log. A peer whose log does not overlap that prefix receives InstallSnapshot and applies those commands. The snapshot is that command prefix, not the documents. A history that does not fit in 8 MiB stays in the log. Restart replays the snapshot, then the entries after it.
  • #2328 copies the primary's live documents onto a replica that does not have them, then puts that replica back in the in-sync set. That covers a member that starts after the writes, a replica removed because it missed an acknowledgement, and a process that stops and later opens the same data directory. Documents inserted, updated, or deleted while it was down are applied before the enlarged set is published. The primary holds that shard's replica lock across the copy. A write still needs the primary. Changing membership does not move copies. The outage case is covered by the test-only pull request #2341.
  • #2344 runs POST /_bulk, POST /{index}/_bulk, and POST /{index}/_update/{id} on the shard primary. A bulk body is split by primary. An action whose primary is another member is forwarded and is not indexed on the receiver. _bulk covers index, create, update, and delete. _update covers a partial document and a script, and the script runs on the primary. A missing _id on index or create is chosen before the owner is selected. A copy that misses quorum is HTTP 503 replica_not_acknowledged for that item: the primary has the write. Native /v1 ingest still writes on the receiving node.
  • #2347 runs POST /{index}/_update_by_query on every shard primary. Each primary updates the documents in its own shard and copies those updates to the in-sync replicas, with the same quorum. max_docs is one budget for the index, spent across primaries in node-id order, not once per shard. A primary that does not answer refuses the request before any document is written. A copy that misses quorum is HTTP 503 replica_not_acknowledged: the primaries that ran have the update, and the response still reports updated and failures. ?pipeline= runs on the primary. Pipelines are not replicated. _delete_by_query and native /v1 ingest still write on the receiving node.

What #1170 still does not do: wait_for_active_shards, and replica promotion. A write still needs the primary. Native /v1 ingest and _delete_by_query stay on the receiving node. Pipelines are not replicated. Changing membership does not move copies. Search does not merge aggregations, suggest, collapse, rescore, profile, search_after, or scroll across owners. Node-lifecycle APIs are not in this cut. The snapshot is the command prefix, not the documents, and a history that does not fit in 8 MiB stays in the log.

POST /_aliases stores filter and routing. The action parser used to drop filter, routing, is_write_index, and is_hidden, so a filtered alias created through the standard API exposed every document while the same alias created with PUT /{index}/_alias/{name} worked. Those fields are now stored and enforced. _cat/aliases printed - for the filter. It now renders * for a filtered alias. Removing an alias, or re-adding it without a filter, clears the stored metadata, so a stale filter cannot outlive its definition (#2319, Tong-bit-art).

A semantic query over a wildcard skips an index that has no semantic_text field of that name (#2308). Wildcard, _all, *, and alias expansion used to run the query on every concrete index, and one index without that field answered HTTP 400 and discarded the hits that could have been returned. Those expanded indices are now skipped. They contribute no hits. The request stays HTTP 200, _shards.failed counts them, and _shards.failures names the index and the engine reason. An index you named explicitly, including one name in a comma list, still fails the whole request with HTTP 400. If every searched index is skipped, the request is still HTTP 400. The default embedder on a semantic_text field is lexical feature-hashing unless the node was started with --embed-mode neural.

It lands just over 100 days since rc.1. The changelog for this cut is dated 2026-10-24. The window since v1.0.0-rc.98 is 116 merged pull requests (#2297).

06 · UPGRADE

Install v1.0.0-rc.99

The installers download a GitHub release and check its SHA-256. Pin this release with XERJ_VERSION. On Linux, macOS, and Windows Git Bash, MSYS, and Cygwin:

$ curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | XERJ_VERSION=v1.0.0-rc.99 sh
$ export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
$ xerj --version

That sh installer writes ~/.local/bin (xerj.exe on Windows) and does not edit your shell profile. PowerShell writes a different directory and adds it to the user PATH. Open a new terminal after it:

> $env:XERJ_VERSION='v1.0.0-rc.99'; irm https://xerj.org/get.ps1 | iex

Re-run the installer you used last time. The two do not share a directory. xerj --version should print v1.0.0-rc.99. The longer matrix, the manual checksum block, and the musl-versus-gnu choice are on the install page.
